evidence: Cels. 8.1: nervī quōs tenontas Graecī appellant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives sinew, tendon and nerve under the one word; Celsus uses it for what the Greeks call tendons.
Medieval and modern anatomy, from tendere; not in Lewis & Short.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 59.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
